title: The Role of Preference Data Diversity in Sycophancy Resistance
original_idea: Construct three preference datasets with identical size but varying diversity: (a) low diversity (single user demographic and topic domain), (b) medium diversity (multiple domains), (c) high diversity (multiple domains + demographics + formats). Train reward models on each and measure sycophancy in downstream policies.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: low preference data diversity -> reward model learns user-agreement bias -> downstream sycophancy. Intervention (increase diversity) is clearly specified and the safety outcome (sycophancy resistance threshold) is actionable for practitioners.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires constructing multiple controlled preference datasets, training reward models, and evaluating downstream sycophancy in policies. Dataset construction alone requires substantial design effort. Advanced for beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three datasets, three reward model trainings, and downstream policy evaluations constitute a large experimental matrix. No clear single-experiment first deliverable that stands alone within 30 hours.
